what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat chronic (long-lasting) hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults and children 3 years and older. Hepatitis C is a viral infection that can damage your liver over time. This combination pill works by blocking the virus from making copies of itself, which helps clear the infection from your body.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with food once a day. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine properly and may reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing at least 30 kg (about 66 lbs) is ONE tablet taken by mouth ONCE daily with food for 8 weeks. Your doctor will determine the right dose and length of treatment based on your specific hepatitis C strain (genotype) and your treatment history. Do not change your dose or stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 18 hours since your scheduled dose time, take it as soon as you remember (with food). If it has been MORE than 18 hours since your scheduled dose time, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time the following day. NEVER take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from moisture, heat, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids (like aluminum or magnesium-containing products such as Maalox or Mylanta) within 4 hours of your dose, as they can reduce how well this medicine works. Do NOT take rifampin (a common antibiotic), St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), or carbamazepine (Tegretol), as these can make Vosevi much less effective. Avoid drinking alcohol excessively, as it can worsen liver damage. Tell ALL of your doctors and pharmacists about every medicine, vitamin, supplement, and herbal product you take, because many drugs can interact with this medication. If you also take rosuvastatin (Crestor) or certain other cholesterol medicines (statins), talk to your doctor, as the combination may increase the risk of muscle problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes (jaundice); dark or tea-colored urine; clay-colored or very light stools; severe tiredness or weakness; nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain that does not go away; confusion or difficulty thinking clearly; slow or irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting (especially if you also take heart rhythm medicines like amiodarone); signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Most people do not feel any different while taking this medicine, but it is working inside your body to fight the hepatitis C virus. After you finish your 8-week course, your doctor will do a blood test about 12 weeks later to check if the virus is no longer detected in your blood. This is called a 'sustained virologic response' (SVR) or a 'cure.' It is very important to take every dose as prescribed and complete the full course of treatment — even if you feel fine — to give yourself the best chance of curing the infection.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine has not been fully studied in pregnant people. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before starting this medicine. If your treatment partner or you use ribavirin alongside any hepatitis C treatment, effective contraception is required. Liver disease: If you have moderate to severe liver disease (Child-Pugh B or C cirrhosis), do NOT take this medicine — it is not safe for you. Kidney disease: Dose adjustment is generally not needed for kidney problems, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Children: This medicine is approved for children 3 years and older who weigh at least 30 kg; use in younger or smaller children has not been established. Older adults (65+): No special dose adjustment is needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
